The engine instead exposes this as a discretionary player action `contestBattlefield`, letting the mover take unrelated Neutral-Open actions between the Move and the contest.

confirmed.notes:
Rule 337.4 states that after all pending Chain Items are finalized, "the controller of the next item on the chain gains Priority" before Step 2: Execute. Items are finalized oldest→newest (337.1.b), so "next item" = the topmost/newest finalized item — the same semantics 340.4 makes explicit ("controller of the newest item on the chain gains Priority"). 

Engine behavior: `fireTriggers` (trigger-runner.ts:270-313) orders simultaneous triggers turn-player-first, then loops `addToChain` for each. In `addToChain` (chain-state.ts:226-227) the first triggered item opens the chain with `activePlayer = item.controller` (turn player); every subsequent triggered item hits the `item.triggered && state.chain?.active` branch and PRESERVES that activePlayer. Net effect: initial priority = controller of the OLDEST/bottom item (always the turn player), not the newest/top item. The comment cites rules 537.1/541.2, which do not exist in the current rulebook (rule.ts returns "no rule matching") — stale references. By contrast, the post-resolve path (chain-state.ts:342-348) correctly sets `activePlayer = items[items.length-1].controller`, so 340.4 is honored.

Post-resolve seq 195/197 correctly assign priority to the new top's controller.

The engine instead leaves the turn in Neutral Open after the move and offers arbitrary main-phase actions — including `endTurn` — while a combat is Staged and no showdown/chain exists.

(c) endTurn.condition only rejects when bf.contested is true (turn.ts:67-71); it does not check for opposing units, so endTurn is legal while Combat is Staged per 461. The real flow hook (riftbound-flow.ts:285-312) mutates VP directly and would not hit the neutral-open gate, so the defect is in the harness/scorePoint interaction, not the core flow logic.

The claim misdiagnoses both the mechanism and the rules.

"reaction" : "action"` and calls `isLegalTiming`. `isLegalTiming("action", closed)` returns false (chain-state.ts:156-162), so a non-Reaction [Add] ability IS rejected in Closed State. The [Add] short-circuit at chain-moves.ts:701-708 is in the reducer (post-legality) and only implements the immediate-resolve behavior; it plays no part in the legality gate. The claim's assertion that "the engine is treating [Add] abilities as activatable at any time" is therefore false — it is treating *Reaction* abilities that way, which is correct.

(3) Rules: 381 states the default. The exemption the claimant looked for under 381.x lives elsewhere: rule 309.1.a ("Only cards and abilities with the Reaction keyword can be played or activated in a Closed State"), rule 813.1+ (Reaction is a Permissive keyword granting "can be activated during Closed States on any player's turn"), rule 429.3 ("Activated abilities that Add resources and have the Reaction tag can be activated at any time that spells or abilities require resources be paid"), and rule 444.2.c (same, "ignoring normal restrictions"). Rule 429.2/429.2.a mandates that Add abilities resolve immediately without priority passing — exactly the nextChainItemId-not-incrementing behavior the claim cited as suspicious.

At seq 150 the scorePoint enumerator (combat.ts:708-729) offered ONLY player-2-bf and excluded player-1-bf. Therefore scoredThisTurn[player-2] contained player-1-bf and did NOT contain player-2-bf — i.e., the Hold scored player-1-bf, not player-2-bf. seq 150 then scored player-2-bf.
